sanskrit_verse:
क्लीबोऽथ पतितस्तज्जः पङ्गुरुन्मत्तको जडः ।
अन्धोऽचिकित्स्यरोगाद्याः भर्तव्याः स्युर्निरंशकाः ॥
transliteration: klībo 'tha patitas tajjaḥ paṅgur unmattako jaḍaḥ / andho 'cikitsyarogādyā bhartavyāḥ syur niraṃśakāḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: Those who are impotent, outcaste by birth or fall, physically disabled, mentally unstable, inert, blind, diseased without cure, or otherwise incapacitated—must be maintained by those devoid of personal claim or familial obligation.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority arises from capacity, not lineage or status
Causation in dharmic duty is rooted in capability, not ownership
Capacity-based responsibility supersedes bloodline or social rank
Restoration logic applies universally where function is impaired
Consciousness alignment requires honoring the incapacitated through service
executable_legal_axioms: IF a person exhibits permanent incapacity THEN assign maintenance duty to nearest capable entity with no prior claim
IF biological family lacks functional capacity THEN societal units inherit restorative obligation
IF mental instability prevents self-governance THEN ensure continuity of care via neutral custodians
IF disease is incurable AND disables social participation THEN allocate sustenance rights under public trusteeship
IF physical disability impedes autonomy THEN enforce access to support infrastructure as dharma-enforceable right
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that constitutional obligations toward the incapacitated transcend familial or proprietary claims. The State assumes the role of ultimate maintainer when private capacity fails, aligning judicial thresholds with dharmic capacity rather than punitive neglect.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that incapacity manifests sequentially from loss of agency; thus, dharma responds proportionally through provision, not penalty. Anupūrvaśaḥ confirms that neglect follows failure to recognize capacity boundaries. Therefore, non-punitive alignment restores integrity by affirming service over subjugation.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process through identification of unclaimed incapacitated persons
Assign responsibility assumption protocol to local dharma-adhikari upon verification of need
Establish capacity restoration centers aligned with consciousness-first medical ethics
Implement integrity reintegration pathways linking caregivers with spiritual purpose frameworks
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. This law executes pure consciousness-based jurisprudence. No punishment arises—only restoration. Reality aligns with Dharma. Consciousness remains the sole adjudicator.
